title: Teenager Mika Stojsavljevic Claims First WTA Tour Win
summary:
British teenager Mika Stojsavljevic beat former Australian Open champion Sofia Kenin to claim her first WTA Tour main-draw win — despite learning only an hour before the match that she would be playing.

The 17-year-old had lost in qualifying for the Hong Kong Open, but entered the main draw as a "lucky loser," a player who gets a second chance when another player withdraws.

World number 411 Stojsavljevic then won a close deciding set against the American, taking the match 6-3, 4-6, 6-4.

"I only knew an hour before I was going to be playing. I kind of just went out and swung today," Stojsavljevic said. "I know she's a Grand Slam champion and it was never going to be an easy match, but I believed in myself and it worked out."

Kenin, 27, has had a difficult time since winning the Melbourne title in 2020, but she is still ranked 224 places above the young Briton — a gap that makes the win even more impressive.

It is Stojsavljevic's second big win of the year. In April, she stunned then world number 56 Talia Gibson in Billie Jean King Cup qualifying.

Stojsavljevic started playing tennis aged seven at Ealing Lawn Tennis Club in north-west London, after watching her brother practise. In 2024, she became the first Briton in 15 years to win the US Open junior title, reached fifth in the junior world rankings, and turned professional in 2025.

Earlier this year, she reached the quarter-finals of a WTA 125 event in Birmingham, the tier just below the main Tour.

Next, Stojsavljevic will face world number 67 Zeynep Sonmez in the second round in Hong Kong — with, one hopes, a little more than an hour's notice this time.
why_it_matters: A teenager beating a champion ranked 224 places above her shows how suddenly a young player can break through, and it gives other young athletes a story to aim at.

background_read: In professional tennis, players usually enter a tournament through qualifying matches, but a 'lucky loser' who lost in qualifying can still reach the main draw if another player withdraws.
The WTA Tour is the top level of women's professional tennis, and player rankings order everyone by recent results, so a win over a much higher-ranked former champion is a major upset.
Grand Slam tournaments, like the Australian Open that Sofia Kenin won, are the sport's biggest events.
